subject: Lighting inside and around cabinetry
hook: Warm white or cool white under the cabinets?
ig:
Warm white or cool white under the cabinets? It changes how the whole kitchen feels.

A: Warm white
A softer, slightly yellow light. Makes oak-effect doors look richer and painted finishes look calm. Lovely in the evening with the main lights off. The trade-off: a touch less crisp when you're doing detailed prep.

B: Cool white
Bright and neutral, closer to daylight. Great for chopping, cleaning and seeing true colours. The trade-off: in the evening it can make a kitchen feel more like a workspace than somewhere to sit.

A tip: look at door samples under both before you decide. A charcoal finish can look very different under each.

Which would you choose — and do you use your kitchen more for cooking or for sitting and chatting? Tell us in the comments.

Sunday question for anyone planning a new kitchen: warm white or cool white under the cabinets?

Warm white is cosy and makes oak-effect and painted doors look lovely in the evening. Cool white is crisper for prep and cleaning, but can feel a bit clinical when the big lights are off.

Our tip: look at your door samples under both before deciding. Charcoal and oak-effect can look surprisingly different.
